title: AI Cloud, Data Platform, and IoT Use Case Design

questions.question: Why do platform constraints matter for AI use cases?
options: Because latency, residency, streaming, and platform dependency can change the architecture
Because every AI use case has the same architecture
Because data boundaries do not matter
Because cloud choice is never relevant
questions.explanation: Platform constraints can determine whether an AI architecture is feasible.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Data residency is a core platform and architecture constraint.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked platform-aware AI use case plan with controls
questions.explanation: The artifact recommends architecture controls for platform-aware use cases.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Data boundaries make platform design accountable.

questions.question: When does an AI use case need architecture review?
options: When technical value and platform risk are high, especially with latency, data residency, streams, or dependencies
Only when the use case has no data
Only when platform constraints are absent
Never; all use cases can use the same pattern
questions.explanation: High-value platform-risk use cases need architecture review.

questions.question: What should be documented before choosing a cloud or platform pattern?
options: Architecture sketch, data boundary, streaming fit, and platform decision
questions.explanation: These controls help teams choose feasible platform designs.
